summary: The note reports on the city's expanded recycling efforts, centered on the Green Horizon Initiative launched on October 3, 2023 under Mayor Susan Krawczyk. It covers community leadership, new sorting technology, the RecycleSmart app, education programs, business and university partnerships, and the remaining challenges such as uneven neighborhood adoption and funding.
one_line: The city's Green Horizon Initiative boosts recycling through technology, education, community leaders, and business and university partnerships, though funding and neighborhood gaps remain.
key_facts: Mayor Susan Krawczyk took office on September 15, 2023 and made improving the city's recycling programs one of her stated goals.
The 'Green Horizon Initiative,' a citywide strategy to improve recycling rates, was inaugurated on October 3, 2023.

Green Horizon is funded by the city budget and grants from environmental organizations, and aims to ease access to recycling facilities, invest in efficient processing technology, and educate the public.
Carlos Rivera, Director of the Green Earth Collective, runs recycling workshops across the city and works with neighborhood councils to identify each area's needs.

Julie Anne, Chief Technology Officer of the city's Waste Management Department, said new sorting machinery uses magnets, infrared sensors, and artificial intelligence to sort recyclables more accurately.
The new sorting technology has decreased contamination rates and improved the quality of recycled materials.
The 'RecycleSmart' app launched on January 22, 2024 and lets users scan items to learn whether they are recyclable and how to dispose of them.
Environmental Educator Sarah Tanaka hosts recycling seminars in schools and community centers, including one demonstrated on February 15, 2024.
'Recycle and Reward' gives citizens discounts and incentives from local businesses for consistently recycling.
Electronics retailer TechTrend partnered with Green Earth Collective to provide ewaste drop-off points at all its city locations, launched March 3, 2024; CEO Jameson Clarke spoke at the event.
Restaurants and cafes have begun using compostable packaging and on-site compost bins to reduce food waste.

The city's university system partners with the city, with research teams optimizing recycling processes and developing easier-to-recycle materials, and sustainability departments running campus-wide recycling.
Challenges remain: some neighborhoods are slow to adopt new practices due to lack of infrastructure or educational resources, and there are financial hurdles to maintaining and expanding systems.
